commands.review_summary:
The PR changes background exec notifyOnExit truncation to use UTF-16-safe helpers and adds regression coverage for surrogate-boundary cuts.

PR surface: Source +2, Tests +33. Total +35 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection plus a read-only string probe show the current raw suffix-cut pattern can start a tail with a lone low surrogate; the PR fixes the main notify path but leaves the same pattern in node-host follow-up output.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair can replace the remaining raw node-host suffix slice with the existing UTF-16-safe helper and add targeted coverage on the PR branch.

target.title: fix(agents): keep background exec exit notifications UTF-16 safe at the snippet cut
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who enable background exec exit notifications (`notifyOnExit`) can receive a broken/replacement character in their chat channel. When completed background command output is trimmed for the `Exec completed/failed (...) :: <output>` notification, either the 400-character tail source or the final 180-character snippet could previously split an emoji's UTF-16 surrogate pair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The notification path now keeps both truncation points UTF-16 safe: the shared `tail()` helper uses `sliceUtf16Safe` for suffix cuts, and the notification snippet compactor uses `truncateUtf16Safe` before appending the ellipsis. ASCII/BMP output and the existing ellipsis behavior are unchanged. Risk is limited to exec output retention/notification strings; this does not change process execution, routing, permissions, or channel transport behavior.

## User Impact

Background exec completion notifications delivered to chat channels no longer show a broken character when emoji output lands at either notification truncation boundary. Ordinary output remains unchanged, and long snippets are still compacted with `…`.

## Evidence

`maybeNotifyOnExit` in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` takes `tail(..., DEFAULT_NOTIFY_TAIL_CHARS)` and then compacts that text before calling `enqueueSystemEvent`, so the defect is in the runtime notification string before any channel transport sees it.

Focused regressions in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts` now cover both boundaries:

- final snippet cut: emoji high surrogate at the 180-character compaction edge
- notify tail source: output longer than 400 characters where the 400-character tail would start inside an emoji

Real runtime proof after this fix, using the actual `runExecProcess` path and real system-event queue (`runExecProcess` -> backgrounded exit -> `enqueueSystemEvent` -> `drainSystemEvents`):

```json
{
  "outcome": "completed",
  "eventCount": 1,
  "notification": "Exec completed (tidal-nu, code 0) :: bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb…",
  "hasLoneSurrogate": false,
  "hasReplacementCharacter": false,
  "includesTailHead": true
}
```

Commands run:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts -t "exec notifyOnExit suppression"` -> pass
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/bash-process-registry.test.ts src/shared/utf16-slice.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts` -> pass
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module ...` real runtime proof above -> pass
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts` -> pass
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/bash-process-registry.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts` -> pass
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` -> pass

What was not tested: no live Telegram/Discord channel round-trip was exercised. The failure and fix are before transport, in the exact system-event text handed to delivery, so the real runtime proof above covers the affected boundary; full broad validation runs in CI.

AI-assisted: implemented and validated with AI assistance; the commands and outputs above were run for real.
